title: Push with an Input Head Move
statement: Let $c$ be a partial recursive program, let $x$ be a finite input string over the bridge alphabet, and let $q,q_m,q'$ be optional control states of its bridging machine. Given a valid input-head position $p$, an assignment $st$ of compiled-machine stacks, an output string, a stack name $k$, a compiled-stack symbol $a$, and a direction $d$, perform two actions on the work tape corresponding to $k$: first move its head one cell left without writing, then write $a$ without moving that work-tape head while moving the input head by $d$. The resulting configuration has state $q'$, input position given by the clamped move of $p$ by $d$, unchanged output, and stack assignment obtained by replacing $st(k)$ with $a$ prepended to it; the intermediate state is $q_m$.
hypotheses_covered: A finite input string over the bridge alphabet
replaced:
Performing the two-action push of a symbol $a$ onto the stack named $k$, where the
second action additionally moves the input head in a direction $d$, transforms a
bridge configuration into the bridge configuration with $a$ prepended to the stack
at $k$ and the input head moved by $d$, the output unchanged.
